basics.name: Zachariah Risheq
basics.summary: MS student in Computer Science at the University of Virginia and a researcher at the LIVE Lab, advised by Prof. Yen-Ling Kuo. My research interests span theory-of-mind (ToM), World Models, and vision-language-action.

highlights: Authored the research proposal on multi-agent reinforcement learning and diffusion models, investigating diffusion models for uncertainty-aware MARL.
Proposed and built a novel decentralized cooperative MARL system coupling MAPPO with a diffusion-based uncertainty signal, trained CTDE in an asymmetric actor-critic framework.
Built a low-dimensional test environment for the collaborative framework.
Improved value estimation by +5% and successful episodes per run by +8% over a baseline PPO policy.

work.summary: Part-time. Charlottesville, VA. Advisor: Prof. Yen-Ling Kuo.
highlights: Built an end-to-end text-to-MuJoCo simulation generation pipeline, synthesizing and reconstructing 3D assets from natural-language scene specifications and automatically generating executable simulation environments.
Proposed and implemented a novel Markov-Chain-Monte-Carlo simulation generation process using a value function for the MDP.
Built a 100 Hz AR teleoperation system on Meta Quest 3, streaming bimanual controller poses to a mobile manipulator over low-latency sockets for scalable robot-demonstration collection.
Collected 100+ demonstrations, 15 hours, and 1000+ trajectories.
Evaluated generated scenes across 100 prompts spanning 25 object classes, achieving 92% executable-scene success and reducing manual environment construction from 30 min to 4 min.
Built a cross-format scene-conversion pipeline exporting model directives to MuJoCo and Unity, plus a post-hoc critic-driven evaluation stage over frozen 3D scenes.

work.summary: Internship. Charlottesville, VA. Advisor: Prof. Nicola Bezzo.
highlights: Led a cross-functional team developing an interactive AR interface in Unity for real-time UAV/UGV trajectory visualization and mission-plan editing.
Developed an LLM/VLM command-grounding service mapping ambiguous natural-language instructions into structured robot trajectory edits and goal specifications.
Evaluated command grounding on 100 instructions, achieving 97.3% execution accuracy and reducing invalid plans by 99%.
Developed a conditional diffusion model for robot costmap and trajectory generation, using value-function-derived supervision from human trajectory edits to adapt future plans.

Built a real-time TCP communication server with 100 Hz communication and length-prefixed framing, integrating a diffusion-model backend, Unity AR client, Vicon motion capture, and a ROSbot UGV into one closed-loop pipeline.

work.summary: Full-time. Charlottesville, VA. Advisor: Prof. Sebastian Elbaum; research assistant to Meriel Von Stein.
highlights: Mentored a cohort of two undergraduates in outdoor autonomous-navigation and data-collection workflows, guiding them to execute 3 km of collision-free field runs and contribute 1000+ labeled frames to the dataset.
Authored a Python data-augmentation toolkit that grew the LiDAR and image corpus 10x and lifted detection recall by 12%.
Reduced preprocessing time by 60% using optimized NumPy/Pandas scripts.
Implemented PyTorch models integrated with ROS 2, improving robot perception by 30%.
Code: https://github.com/zachkr05/ROSbot_data_collection - ROS workspace for collecting human navigation data of a Husarion ROSbot 2.0.

education.institution: University of Virginia, School of Engineering

publications.name: GuidAR: Meta-Learned MoE Diffusion Costmaps From AR Trajectory Edits
publications.publisher: Undergraduate Senior Thesis, University of Virginia (UVA Libra)
publications.summary: Z. Risheq, N. Bezzo, E. Travis. Learns diffusion costmaps from human trajectory edits made in augmented reality, so a single correction generalizes to the robot's future plans.

portfolio.name: GuidAR: Diffusion Costmaps From Human AR Trajectory Edits
portfolio.description: A mixture-of-experts conditional diffusion model that learns robot costmaps from trajectory edits a person makes in augmented reality.

highlights: Evaluated student teams (ages 9-14) on project innovation, core values, and robot design at regional FLL competitions.
Facilitated structured interviews and provided constructive feedback to encourage STEM learning and teamwork.
Collaborated with a panel of judges to deliberate and award recognitions based on FIRST's judging rubrics and values.
